A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison after matching reorganized material.

before.justification: v1 reports original transformer experiments on synthetic Markov sequences, architectural and data ablations, and numerical simulations of regression gradient flow.

after.justification: v2 retains these original results and adds comparisons of simplified theoretical trajectories with full regression flow and classification-transformer dynamics.

M1.justification: The full and minimal transformers, training objectives, and gradient-flow systems are retained. The rewritten representational construction clarifies and corrects the mathematical description rather than introducing a new training or inference procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use synthetic Markov classification and positional regression, retaining finite/online data, reversed importance, non-uniform weights, and overlapping-interval scenarios. The new diagnostics examine these existing tasks.

E2.justification: v2 Figure 7 adds simplified stage-wise ODE trajectories as an explicit internal comparator to the full regression flow; v1 plotted only the full-flow trajectories. The restricted-context transformer comparators remain unchanged.

E3.justification: The new Appendix D comparison initializes simplified ODEs at t = 25 and t = 300 and compares attention mass and value-matrix alignments. It also measures corresponding alignments in the classification transformer. Existing data and training settings in Tables 1–4 are unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix D adds direct tests of whether the simplified dynamics track full regression flow and whether classification transformers exhibit the predicted value-matrix compensation (Figures 7–8). These substantially extend validation of the central mechanism. The original regression simulation and ablation suite are retained, not newly introduced.

E5.justification: Both versions list seed 0 and retain the same reporting practice. Neither introduces repeated-run summaries, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests.

E6.justification: The original experimental curves are retained. Figures 7–8 add theoretical-versus-simulated trajectories and classification value-alignment results; Section 2.5 also newly reports persistence of the attention hierarchy during overfitting with 600 samples. These are additional findings, not revised same-setting performance scores.

T1.justification: New Appendix A constructs equivalent logits using overlapping weighted decompositions. v2 also corrects Theorem 3's deviation definition and restores the factor m2* in Theorem 4's limiting value matrix. The main convergence theorems and proof arguments otherwise remain substantially unchanged.

C1.justification: Incremental sparse attention and competitive-to-cooperative dynamics remain the central contributions. v2 narrows the headline framing: the definite early-stopping regularization claim and broad reasoning implications give way to a controlled surrogate account and a suggested connection to effective complexity.

C2.justification: v2 adds substantive interpretations concerning non-identifiability and sparse-solution selection, the roles of isotropy and orthogonality, and hierarchical attention despite feature overfitting. It also explicitly distinguishes quantitative comparisons within regression from qualitative comparisons with classification transformers, clarifying the theory's applicability.

D1.justification: The documented code repository changes from ralvarezlucend/IL-SAP-Transformers to tml-epfl/sparse-attention-dynamics. Appendix D provides restart times and procedures for the new ODE comparison. Existing architecture, optimizer, data, and seed tables are retained.

R1.justification: Section 4 substantially expands positioning against multi-head attention analyses and distinguishes head-level competition from competition between algorithmic circuits. New connections include Chen et al.'s multi-head softmax analysis, Varre and Flammarion's associative recall work, and work by Reddy, Park et al., and Chakrabarti and Balachundar; these go beyond bibliographic updates.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, contribution list, empirical exposition, and conclusion receive extensive rewriting. The representation section moves before the learning experiments, and the appendices are substantially reorganized, separating theoretical validation from the retained experimental details and ablations.

P2.justification: v2 adds multipanel Figures 7–8, expands several captions, and resizes or repositions retained figures and tables. Most original plot content is preserved, including v1 Figure 10 becoming v2 Figure 6.

improvement.justification: v2 makes the central mechanism easier to assess through the new trajectory comparisons, corrects localized theorem statements, and more clearly separates surrogate guarantees from qualitative transformer evidence. The rewritten exposition and research positioning improve clarity. These are useful refinements to an already supported central result, while the underlying empirical coverage and proof framework remain largely unchanged.
